newsitem.title: USA: Argentine banks' ADRs rebound in New York.
newsitem.headline: Argentine banks' ADRs rebound in New York.

text.p: Argentine banks' American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) rebounded in New York Tuesday, boosted by signs of low U.S. inflation, traders said.
ADRs in Banco Frances rose 1-1/4 to 27-1/2 in heavy volume. Banco de Galicia rose 37/64 to 22-5/8.
"This basically because of the rally in the U.S. bond market," a trader said. "They have been hit significantly in the last week or so."
Argentine stocks, especially those of banks, are affected by U.S. interest rates in part because the currency is pegged to the dollar.
Banco Frances has fallen from 31 on March 25, when the U.S. central bank raised interest rates. Banco de Galicia has dropped from 25-1/2 since then.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was up 1-2/32 to yield 7.08 after the Labor Department's Consumer Price Index for March came in lower than expected.
